profile.headline: at Navitas Solutions Inc.
profile.summary: I have extensive experience in embedded firmware coding, software development, team management, and new business development. I have in-depth knowledge in digital signal processing field including statistical signal processing, time-series analysis, and speech signal processing. I am also interested in detection and estimation theories such as Kalman filtering. More recently, I enjoy applying the advanced machine learning and deep learning algorithms to various time-based digital signals including speech and financial data

positions.title: Chief Software Engineer
positions.description:
Navitas Solutions developed a new automotive battery management systems (BMS) using wireless communication. 

My role included planning, specifying, coding, executing, evaluating, and documenting tests of requirements. While actively participating in embedded firmware coding, I also managed the entire software/firmware development cycle complying with the automotive functional safety standard ISO-26262 and MISRA C - 2004 coding standards. 

Notable Results:
•	Developed embedded battery management system (BMS) software on 8051-based and ARM-based MCUs. Designed and implemented the Wireless Battery Area Network (WiBaAN) protocol, which is Navitas’ proprietary wireless communication protocol for wireless battery management system (WiBMS).
•	Developed algorithms estimating State of Charge (SOC) and State of Health (SOH) for Lithium-Ion Batteries for electrical vehicles using extended Kalman filters (EKF), fuzzy, and recurrent neural network (RNN) algorithms.
•	Brought the products to the SODW and Advanced technology (AT) projects with major automotive manufacturers (OEMs) in the US and Europe.
•	Helped secure three rounds of funding (seed, series A and B) of $16 millions.

positions.title: Senior Software Architect
positions.description:
AMR Inc. was a defense contractor working with U.S. federal government including Department of Defense (U.S. Air Force, and Navy), NASA, NSF and Department of Energy (DOE). 

I was successfully awarded two DoD SBIR contracts and developed a new voice transformation platform called MagicTTSTM. By modifying an input speech, the software can create an infinite number of new character voices, with different speaking styles (including military "radio voice") and speaking speeds. The platform incorporated various digital signal processing technologies including speech synthesis, voice transformation and time-scale modification technologies.

Notable Results;
•	Awarded and successfully completed a US Air Force SBIR contract as Primary Investigator (Phase I and Phase II), “Voice Transformation and Detection”
•	Awarded and successfully completed a US Navy SBIR contract as Primary Investigator (Phase I and Phase II), “Variable Speed Speech Synthesis”

positions.title: Member of Technical Staff
positions.description:
While working for the Bell Labs, I participated in two projects: (1) Bell Labs Voice Recognition and Text-to-Speech (TTS) system, and (2) Voice over IP system for  CDMA 2000 EVDO Rev. A.

For the Bell Labs Voice Recognition and TTS system, I conducted basic research on digital speech signal processing methods for prosody modification and large-corpus based unit-selection methods. I also conducted research on new content-based multimedia search/retrieval algorithms. 

For the Voice over IP system, I conducted basic research on next generation wireless communication system including a new virtual jitter buffer management algorithm which can reduce the end-to-end delay without any voice quality degradation. I also conducted research on VoIP quality improvement, QOS measurement, especially for wireless communication. 

My contributions resulted in numerous peer reviewed papers and patents.

Notable Results;
•	Invented virtual jitter buffer management scheme, packet loss concealment and decoder resynchronization for Voice over IP for wireless communication. – Contributions to 3GPP, 3GPP2, and ITU.
•	Developed a reduced delay and low complexity ITU_T G.711 Packet Loss Concealment
•	Developed a prototype all-IP Media Server
•	Improved vocoder based speech prosody algorithm by introducing the concept of mixed-phase into the cepstrum analysis.
•	Incorporated the Residual PSOLA algorithm into the Bell Labs' multilingual Text-to-Speech product.
•	Bell Labs was awarded the 48th technical Grammy by the Recording Academy in 2006 – invited to the Grammy award ceremony.
